rounds.text: Adroit Infotech Ltd is trading at an attractive valuation with a price-to-book ratio of 0.68x against a book value of ₹ 13.1 [E1], and a sector benchmark price-to-book of 3.08x compared to the company's 0.58x [E6]. The business demonstrates real cash generation capability, posting a positive operating cash flow of Rs 2.28 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs 2.25 Cr in March 2026 [E31, E32]. This fundamental strength is reinforced by recent internal confidence, as promoter holdings increased by 4.71% over the last quarter [E51]. Furthermore, the company operates within an Information Technology sector that enjoys a supportive macro tailwind with a tailwind score of up to +0.66 [E64, E65]. Conceded: [E13], [E26], [E56].

Adroit Infotech Ltd carries severe fundamental flaws that make its low valuation a trap rather than a bargain. Compounded sales growth has contracted across 10, 5, 3, and trailing twelve-month periods, culminating in a sharp 28% drop in recent sales [E13, E14, E15, E16]. Profitability metrics are deeply depressed, featuring a negative return on equity of -1.0% and a multi-year operating margin trend that has steadily decreased over the last four years to -36% [E12, E26, E28]. Furthermore, balance sheet health is deteriorating as borrowings jumped to Rs 25.66 Cr from Rs 14.57 Cr a year earlier, contributing to a flagged low interest coverage ratio [E35, E52]. Operational efficiency is alarmingly poor, highlighted by excessively high debtors of 514 days and earnings that rely on Rs 3.66 Cr of other income [E55, E56]. Market confidence reflects these underlying weaknesses through a weak relative-strength rating of 27, a severe historical drawdown of 94.5%, and a rules-based screen score of 34 out of 100 yielding a medium-confidence sell signal [E42, E44, E58]. Conceded: [E6].

Conceded: [E13], [E14], [E15], [E16], [E26], [E28], [E35], [E52], [E55], [E56], [E42], [E44], and [E58]. However, the bear paints a one-sided picture by ignoring tangible improvements and fundamental support. The company generated positive operating cash flow of Rs 2.28 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 2.25 Cr in Mar 2026 [E31, E32]. Furthermore, the valuation trades at a deep discount with a price-to-book of 0.68x [E1] and a heavily discounted P/B of 0.58x against a sector benchmark of 3.08x [E6]. Finally, promoter holding has recently increased by 4.71% over the last quarter [E51], and the broader Information Technology sector is enjoying a strong macro tailwind [E64, E65].

Conceded: [E31] and [E32]. The bull points to positive operating cash flow of Rs 2.28 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 2.25 Cr in Mar 2026, but this overlooks the severe quality issues in those earnings, notably that the company relies on Rs 3.66 Cr of other income [E55] to flatter results while suffering from a staggering 514-day debtor backlog [E56]. While the bull highlights a deep discount with a price-to-book of 0.68x [E1] and a sector-relative P/B of 0.58x against 3.08x [E6], this low valuation is entirely justified by a multi-year structural decay, including a 10-year sales contraction of -7% [E13], a -28% drop in trailing sales [E16], and a dismal rules-based screen score of 34 out of 100 pointing to a sell rating [E58]. The bull's citation of a recent 4.71% quarterly promoter holding increase [E51] completely ignores the broader longer-term insider divestment trend of -7.02% over the last 3 years [E57]. Finally, while the Information Technology sector enjoys a macro tailwind [E64, E65], Adroit Infotech fails to capitalize on it, lagging the market with an anemic relative-strength rating of 27 [E42] and a history of extreme volatility and a 94.5% peak-to-trough drawdown [E44].
